chapter: War years, Goodman and Woody Herman
title: Goodman's perfectionism and fear in his band
summary: Dance explains that Benny, a perfectionist, expected everyone to be as great as he was, which made sidemen scared.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Well Red, I'm not saying this in -- in an attempting to be slighting Benny anyway, because you know, I was always very interested in Benny's band, starting with the first one, which I was closely connected with.
I know. I know.

And it was a wonderful band and it kept on developing, but I think the thing -- you know, I always felt sorry for Benny because he's a perfectionist and can't help himself and this is what made things so difficult in his band. I mean he'd give people the ray and everything, but he couldn't help himself.

Oh, I found this with Benny Goodman. Most of the guys that wanted to play all the time, I didn't think he had trouble with in those periods. Those years. I -- couple of guys I know in the band, I recommended to him. That was -- were not the best acting guys, I was a little ashamed that I'd recommended, but they said 'Oh, this music,' and they had a lot of things to think about and they'd slunch over on the band stand --
Oh, yeah.
-- and they really wasn't getting in in trying time to play well.
Yeah. Anybody's going to mind that.
And I think it aggravated Benny, because I --
Yeah.
-- and it would me, too.
Sure.
If I was a leader I'd say, if you want to play, fine. If you don't, then leave.
Yeah.
So when you talk about the ray I think that -- we never had one word in the sextet, we always tried to go down --
Yeah.
-- we played it and he knew it.
Yeah.
We all knew it.
Yeah.
Ah --

No, well that thing I'm thinking about, anyway, Red, that's not quite the same thing, it wasn't so much that any of the trouble that I knew of in the band, wasn't so much the way guys were acting, or anything, but many guys that were working with Benny were scared.
Yeah.

Because nobody was on a par with Benny's talents. And you know that he couldn't help being demanding, because the thing I felt about Benny was, I always felt that Benny never recognized that people didn't have as -- he always thought everybody should be great. Just -- he was great and he didn't think too much of it, really. I don't consider that he was a very conceited guy or anything. He had this great talent, he kind of thought that that's how everybody should have a talent like that. And he'd look at guys as much to say, what's
the matter with you. And they were thinking, My God, I mean, you know, a lot of the guys in the band were scared. Well in the early days they were.
